The general problem of the determination of geodetics on any surface may be advantageously treated in connexion with that of “parallel” curves. By “parallel” curves are meant curves whose geodetic distances from one another are constant—in other words, the orthogonal trajectories of a system of geodetics. In applying this method the determination of a system of parallel curves comes first, and the determination of the geodetics to which they are orthogonal follows as a deduction.
